content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text rules on a link collision over Isaiah 7:14 in which the parties' chains are pressed against one another, so K-C's chain-versus-chain requirement governs it.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "\"weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse\": reading one requires evaluating the whole chains and their footings; reading two allows splitting separately answered aspects and declaring underdetermination without a chain-by-chain footing comparison.", "why": "The judge does not weigh the two chains by their footings; it instead separates the challenger's wording answer from the defender's application answer and declares the point underdetermined."}
